title: Are Appliance Extended Warranties Worth It in 2026?
summary: An appliance dealer's CEO explains that most extended warranties disappoint because claims route to disconnected call centers, and gives failure-rate data for which categories are worth covering.

assertions.quote: You call a call center, not a service department, and they route it to the lowest-cost technician in your area

verdicts.note: Consistent with industry structure described by a dealer with 33,000 annual service calls and matches complaint patterns elsewhere.

assertions.quote: Above 25%, the plan reliably costs more than the repairs it is meant to cover

verdicts.note: A reasonable rule of thumb from one dealer's internal data, not an independently verified industry-wide threshold.

Abito & Salant find extended warranties priced on average at 24% of the insured product's price ("roughly a quarter"), but even at that typical price point the estimated profit margin is already 62%-73% -- the product looks like a poor deal near or below the claim's stated quarter-of-price threshold, not only once priced above it.

assertions.quote: a plan you paid $300 for can cost you another $200 to use

verdicts.note: A commonly reported structural feature across both auto and appliance plans.

assertions.quote: Front-load washers, gas ranges and most dishwashers. All sit at or below our 8.3% average

verdicts.note: Reported from the dealer's own service-call data across thousands of repairs.

assertions.quote: Buying before delivery also costs less than buying after

verdicts.note: A standard pricing practice described by the source.
